requirements.requirement: At least four cells forming a tray
requirements.evidence: Built 4-piece cluster: piece:0,0,0;full (central), piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full — compact 4-cell tray, joints locked with jointBolts.

requirements.requirement: Each cell fitted with a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Four hex-bin-full-drain bins installed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full-drain — full-depth trays with drain holes in each cell.

All four bins filled with soil and planted with seedlings (basil-seedling x2, parsley-seedling, lettuce-butterhead-seedling) — props visible from above, demonstrating seed-starting use. meshClash clear, caps applied.

finish.summary: Four-cell hexagonal seed-starting tray built with a drained bin in every cell. Each bin is a full-depth drained type (hex-bin-full-drain) and has been filled with soil and planted with seedlings to demonstrate function. Joints locked and open faces capped; checks clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
